title: How would you estimate what UK families spend on school uniforms each year?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "What do UK families spend on school uniforms each year?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: A two-step estimate with a sensible average that blends cheaper primary and pricier secondary uniforms. Have a go at your own estimate before reading on.
body:
The question

What do UK families spend on school uniforms each year?

The approach

Pupils × spend per pupil per year.

Tip: Before giving the answer, check it from a second direction. It is the step most candidates skip.

Step by step

  1. School pupils in the UK: 10M
  2. × £200 uniform spend per pupil per year

That gives about £2B a year.

Does it make sense?

Secondary uniforms with logos cost more than primary ones, so the average sits between the two.

New-year purchases dominate a seasonal market

The £2 billion estimate assumes £200 of annual spending for each of 10 million pupils. But a pupil's spending varies by school stage, uniform rules, growth and second-hand availability. One child may need a whole new set of clothing; another may only replace shoes and a jumper.

Suppose half of pupils spend £120 annually and the other half spend £280. The weighted average is still £200 per pupil, showing how the original shortcut could arise from two different groups. If the expensive segment is smaller than expected, the market shrinks quickly.

The timing matters for retailers. A large share of annual demand may occur before the school year, so stockouts in a few weeks can cost much more than slow sales in January. Define whether shoes, sports kits and accessories are inside the question before estimating revenue.
